title: Up To My Shoulder
subject: a Mississippi Delta man noodling for a flathead catfish under a cypress log in the Sunflower River with his bare arm, and the forty-one-pound fish that bites back
caption: Raw acoustic Mississippi Delta blues in the pre-war juke-joint style, as revived in the mid-2020s. A metal-bodied resonator guitar played with a bottleneck slide in open G, the thumb thumping a droning bass string; a cupped, overblown harmonica answering each line; a heel stomping a loose shuffle on wooden boards; a low upright bass entering in the last verse. Dry, close-miked room with floor creak and a little bleed. Male baritone, gravelly and hollering, with bent blue notes, moans and a hummed refrain. 84 BPM, G major. Sweaty, boastful and rueful. No drum kit, no electric guitar, no rock beat, no gospel choir, no modern R&B polish.
lyrics:
[Intro - bottleneck slide guitar and foot stomp, hummed]

[Verse 1]
Sunflower River running low and brown as tea
Sunflower River running low and brown as tea
There's a flathead under that cypress log, and he's been waiting just for me

[Pre-Chorus]
Took my boots off, told my cousin, hold my hat

[Chorus]
I'm going in up to my shoulder, Lord
River up to my chin
That fish has got a mouth like a mailbox
And I'm fixing to put my whole arm in

[Verse 2]
Felt along that cypress where the water's cool and black
Felt along that cypress where the water's cool and black
Something grabbed me by the wrist like a screen door slamming back

[Chorus]
I'm in it up to my shoulder, Lord
River up to my chin
Forty pounds of flathead holding on
And I can't tell who's reeling who in

[Verse 3 - upright bass enters]
Weighed him at the bait shop, forty-one and a quarter
Weighed him at the bait shop, forty-one and a quarter
My arm looks like a chewed-up dog toy, and I'm going back for his daughter

[Instrumental Break - harmonica]

[Chorus]
I'll be in up to my shoulder, Lord
Come Saturday again
My wife says buy a rod and reel like a normal man
I say, then how'm I gonna shake hands with his kin

[Outro - hummed, slide fading]
Mm, Sunflower River, mm
